reportSubtitle: Quieter Week After Two Record Highs — Reading It as Normal Variance
summary:
We saw a dip this week, which isn't surprising after two back-to-back best-ever weeks. At 5 to 8 leads per week, this is the kind of swing you expect to see now and then.

Zooming out, the 3-week picture on Lookalike Video still looks healthy: 13 leads at a $23 blended CPL across that window, even with this week included. Most of the CPL jump traces back to the Apr 25 budget bump on that ad set (from $12.50 to $20/day), which usually triggers Meta to spend a few days re-learning before settling back in. The site funnel was a bit lighter across the board too (170 visitors vs 217, 14 modal opens vs 35, paid-tier mix at 12.5%), which reads more like a lower-intent traffic mix this week than anything broken on the page.

We'll chat Monday about a few ideas to keep momentum going. Top of the list: launching the high-spender Lookalike audience, refreshing the creative, and tightening up the funnel form for a smoother experience.

metrics.label: Ad Spend
metrics.note: Flat vs $346.41 last week. New allocation paced as expected.

metrics.label: Leads (Demo Bookings)
metrics.note: Down from 8 last week. 3 of 5 still came from Lookalike Video.

metrics.label: Cost per Lead
metrics.note: Up from $43.30 last week. Lookalike Video drove most of the swing after its Apr 25 budget bump.

metrics.label: Paid-Tier Signup Share
metrics.note: 1 of 8 plan signup clicks landed on a paid tier (1 Pro). Down from 48% last week.

charts.title: Ad Set Performance, This Week (Apr 25 to May 1)

data.note: Daily budget increased from $12.50 to $20 effective Apr 25. Higher spend at lower lead volume drove the CPL spike.

charts.title: Plan Signup Clicks by Tier (7-Day)
charts.note: Just 12.5% of self-serve interest landed on a paid tier this week (1 of 8), down from 48% the prior week. Creator tier saw zero clicks for the first time since tracking started.

findings.title: Lookalike Video CPL Move Lines Up With the Apr 25 Budget Bump
findings.description: 3 leads on $141.95 spend vs 6 leads on $84.75 last week. The daily budget went from $12.50 to $20 (a 60% jump) on Apr 25, well past the ~20% threshold that typically pushes Meta back into a short re-learning period. That usually resolves within a week. Zooming out, the ad set has produced 13 of 22 post-restructure leads across the last 3 weeks at a blended $23.43 CPL, so the underlying engine still looks healthy.

findings.title: Softening Was Site-Wide, Not Isolated to One Ad Set
findings.description: Unique visitors to /enterprise dropped from 217 to 170 (down 22%), modal opens dropped from 35 to 14 (rate from 16.1% to 8.2%), and plan signup clicks dropped from 21 to 8. Lookalike Static and Interest Production Video also had quiet weeks (1 lead each, $106 and $105 CPL). When volume and conversion rates move down together across multiple ad sets, it usually points to a lower-intent traffic mix for the week rather than anything broken on the page or a single audience drying up.

actions.title: Held the Apr 25 Reallocation Through the Full Week
actions.description: Lookalike Video ran at $20/day, Lookalike Static at $15/day, Interest Production Video at $15/day, Interest Production Static stayed paused. Total daily budget held at $50. No mid-week intervention.

actions.title: SMS Reminder System Still Awaiting Decision
actions.description: Proposed Apr 23. Will follow up at the Monday meeting after Anna's honeymoon. No new movement this week.

nextSteps: Build the high-spender Lookalike audience this week so it can launch alongside the Week 9 report on May 8
Use Monday's meeting to align on the high-spender launch, creative refresh ideas, smoothing out the funnel form, and the SMS reminder decision
